name: LinkShell
description: Remote terminal and coding-agent workspace for your phone and browser.

paragraphs: Claude Code, Codex and other coding agents keep running on your computer. From your phone you watch them work live, send a message any time, approve what they ask for, and hand the session back to your terminal when you sit down again. Your code and the agent processes never leave your machine, and the connection is end-to-end encrypted. Supports iPhone Duo, standard iPhones and Android.
Replies stream word by word; plans, tool calls and diffs update live. When it needs permission, or wants you to choose, the request comes to the phone: allow or deny in one tap.

Messages sent mid-turn queue above the composer: reorder, take one back to rewrite, or send it now, straight into the running turn. Stop works on a turn running on the computer too. The session can have been opened in a terminal or in a desktop app.

requirements.text: LinkShell 2.3.33 adds an independently connected watchOS app: sign in with an existing email/password account or enter a computer's pairing code to view sessions, handle simple approvals and send short messages. iPhone companion mode remains available.
Drag into Applications, open and sign in.
The Mac overview and Devices page can generate a pairing QR code and six-digit code; pairing without an account uses a self-hosted gateway.
Codex supports ChatGPT login, API keys and custom providers, including configuration managed by CC Switch; a Codex login is not required by LinkShell.
